To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a simple and practical approach for tracking and visualising student effort can be used by teachers in secondary school to provide a basis for dialogue with students about their learning.

The use of a simple visualisation of student effort, in the form of a "heat map", is a practical way for teachers to engage with the concept of "effort" and to assess student effort in a way that is meaningful to them.
A practical analytics tool for tracking student effort has been developed and deployed in successive versions in secondary school settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing practical tools that can be used by teachers to support their students, and which can be used as a basis for professional development.
how we can use technology to help teachers to help students to learn, by tracking and visualising the qualities that are important to both.
the practical application of analytics to the improvement of learning and teaching, in particular the use of data to support the development of student qualities such as motivation and effort.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach described in this paper has proved effective in practice.
the effort tracker is a valuable tool that is being used in practice by staff and students to support their engagement with learning and teaching.
the approach described here is practical, and can provide useful insights for both students and teachers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has been a successful experiment in the use of learning analytics to support teacher professional development and to improve the learning experience of students.
it has been a success, but that the journey is far from complete.
the analytics are useful to teachers, and that the teachers are useful to the analytics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the iterative refinement of analytics tools is an effective way to build staff engagement and capacity, and to deliver practical insights for students.
the most effective approach to this is to build a tool that can be used by teachers as part of their daily practice.

the iterative development of a visual analytics tool for staff, and the professional development of teachers in using it, can provide a basis for a productive dialogue between staff and students about the qualities of learning that matter.
